{{short description|Triangle center}}

In [[geometry]], the '''congruent isoscelizers point''' is a special point associated with a plane [[triangle]]. It is a [[triangle center]] and it is listed as ''X''(173) in [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]]. This point was introduced to the study of triangle geometry by Peter Yff in 1989.<ref name=ETC>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=X(173) = Congruent isoscelizers point |url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers |access-date=3 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419171900/http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html |archive-date=19 April 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Congruent isoscelizers point|url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/recent/conisos.html|access-date=3 June 2012}}</ref> 

==Definition==
[[File:Congruent isoscelizers point.svg|thumb|300px|<math>\overline{P_1Q_1} = \overline{P_2Q_2} = \overline{P_3Q_3}</math>]]
An [[isoscelizer]] of an angle {{mvar|A}} in a triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} is a line through points {{math|''P''<sub>1</sub>}} and {{math|''Q''<sub>1</sub>}}, where {{math|''P''<sub>1</sub>}} lies on {{mvar|AB}} and {{math|''Q''<sub>1</sub>}} on {{mvar|AC}}, such that the triangle {{math|△''AP''<sub>1</sub>''Q''<sub>1</sub>}} is an isosceles triangle. An isoscelizer of angle {{mvar|A}} is a line perpendicular to the bisector of angle {{mvar|A}}. 

Let {{math|△''ABC''}} be any triangle. Let {{math|''P''<sub>1</sub>''Q''<sub>1</sub>, ''P''<sub>2</sub>''Q''<sub>2</sub>, ''P''<sub>3</sub>''Q''<sub>3</sub>}} be the isoscelizers of the angles {{mvar|A, B, C}} respectively such that they all have the same length. Then, for a unique configuration, the three isoscelizers {{math|''P''<sub>1</sub>''Q''<sub>1</sub>, ''P''<sub>2</sub>''Q''<sub>2</sub>,  ''P''<sub>3</sub>''Q''<sub>3</sub>}} are concurrent. The point of concurrence is the ''congruent isoscelizers point'' of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref name=ETC/>

==Properties==
[[File:Construction for congruent isoscelizers point.svg|thumb|300px|Construction for congruent isoscelizers point. 
{{legend-line|solid black|Reference triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid red|Congruent isoscelizers of {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid cyan|[[Incircle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid green|[[Intouch triangle]] {{math|△''A'B'C' ''}} of {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid blue|Incircle of {{math|△''A'B'C' ''}} (used to construct {{math|△''A"B"C"''}})}}
{{legend-line|dashed black 2px|Perspective lines between {{math|△''ABC''}} and {{math|△''A"B"C"''}}}}
]]
*The [[trilinear coordinates]] of the congruent isoscelizers point of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} are<ref name=ETC/>

<math display=block>\begin{array}{ccccc}
  \cos\frac{B}{2} + \cos\frac{C}{2} - \cos\frac{A}{2} &:& \cos\frac{C}{2} + \cos\frac{A}{2} - \cos\frac{B}{2} &:& \cos\frac{A}{2} + \cos\frac{B}{2} - \cos\frac{C}{2} \\[4pt]
  = \quad \tan\frac{A}{2} + \sec\frac{A}{2} \quad \ \ &:& \tan\frac{B}{2} + \sec\frac{B}{2} &:& \tan\frac{C}{2} + \sec\frac{C}{2}
\end{array}</math>

*The [[intouch triangle]] of the intouch triangle of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} is [[Perspective (geometry)|perspective]] to {{math|△''ABC''}}, and the congruent isoscelizers point is the [[perspector]]. This fact can be used to locate by geometrical constructions the congruent isoscelizers point of any given {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref name=ETC/>
